title: I can't code. Over two days, I directed an AI to build a complete roguelike: Bingo Patch, v1.0 is out (free)
author: Fuujibayashi_74
selftext:
Hi r/aigamedev!

I'm a project manager, not a programmer. Bingo Patch is the game I directed and an AI built: Claude Code wrote every line of code and made the art, the sound and the music... with code. It took two days from the first commit to v1.0, and it's out now on itch.io, free (pay what you want).

THE GAME

A roguelike bingo deckbuilder. You play on a little handheld console that's still in development: each night is a new version (v0.1, v0.2...), each night ends with a bug (the boss), and every bug you fix installs a patch that changes the rules for the rest of the run. Ship v1.0 to win.

\- Place balls on a 5×5 grid you upgrade, complete patterns, score Points × Boost

\- 60 charms, 46 gadgets, special balls (explosive, ghost, glitch...), 30 patches, 20 bugs

\- Even the music updates: a beeper at v0.1, the full band at v1.0, a corrupted version during bugs

HOW WE WORKED

\- Me: the idea, the direction, playtesting every build, feedback in plain French

\- The AI: the code, design proposals, balancing, every text in French and English

\- LÖVE (Lua), about 24,000 lines. No image or audio files: every visual is drawn by code and shaders, and every sound, including 13 music stems, is synthesized when the game starts

WHAT MADE IT WORK

1. Tests the AI runs on its own work. 221 unit tests, a QA bot that drives the real game (137 checks), and a bot that plays thousands of simulated runs for balancing. Before release, it screenshotted every screen in both languages and fixed every text that overflowed.

2. A decision log. 41 design decisions written down, so settled questions don't get reopened from one session to the next.

3. Feedback in plain words. "The mega-combo flames look too much like Balatro" turned into a console that overheats. "The music could be better" turned into four short previews to listen to before anything went into the game.

4. Hard rules from day one. All art and sound generated by code, nothing taken from other games, everything kept in the project folder.

What it can't do alone: tell whether it's fun. That still takes a human playing it, again and again.

Free on itch.io: https://voxnovalys-studio.itch.io/bingo-patch (Windows, English and French)

Happy to answer questions about the workflow, and I'd love your feedback on the game!
